facts.text: Module-level client configuration is removed in v1. Bare module-level attribute assignments `openai.api_key = ...`, `openai.api_base = ...`, and `openai.organization = ...` no longer configure the client and must be replaced by constructing an explicit client object, e.g. `client = OpenAI(api_key=...)`.

All module-level namespaced call patterns of the form `openai.<Namespace>.create(...)` are removed in v1 and must migrate to client-based calls, e.g. `openai.ChatCompletion.create(...)` becomes `client.chat.completions.create(...)`.

The equivalent module-level namespaced `.list(...)` and `.retrieve(...)` calls (i.e. `openai.<Namespace>.list(...)`, `openai.<Namespace>.retrieve(...)`) are likewise removed in v1 and must become client-based calls.

Specific removed module-level call sites named in the guide include `openai.ChatCompletion.create(...)`, `openai.Completion.create(...)`, `openai.Embedding.create(...)`, `openai.Image.create(...)`, and `openai.Moderation.create(...)`.
The `openai.error` submodule is removed in v1. Any reference to `openai.error.*` needs to change.

Exception classes that used to live in `openai.error` now live at the top level of the `openai` package: e.g. `openai.error.RateLimitError` → `openai.RateLimitError`, and likewise `openai.error.ServiceUnavailableError`, `openai.error.InvalidRequestError`, `openai.error.AuthenticationError`, etc.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE (do not flag): response-object access patterns. Whether code reads a response via dict-style access (`response['choices']`) or attribute-style access (`response.choices`), both remain valid; this migration does not touch that.
The listed items are the ONLY confirmed breaking changes in this migration; anything not described in the guide is unaffected.
Affected sites include those reached indirectly through a repository's own helper functions — call chains must be traced, not just the entry-point file grepped.
